walkthroughs.body_html:
Carbon cycle: Photosynthesis removes CO2; respiration, combustion and decay return it.

Water cycle: evaporation → condensation → precipitation → run-off back to the sea.

Nitrogen cycle: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria turn N2 into nitrates. Nitrifying bacteria turn ammonia into nitrates. Decomposers release ammonia from dead matter. Denitrifying bacteria return N2 to the air.

Humans damage ecosystems in big ways.

Deforestation releases stored CO2, destroys habitats and lowers biodiversity.

Climate change (from CO2 and methane) shifts habitats, melts ice, and pushes species towards extinction.

Eutrophication: fertilisers run into rivers → algal bloom → algae die → bacteria use up oxygen → fish suffocate. 🌍

To protect biodiversity, scientists use:

Protected areas (national parks, reserves) — safe habitats.

Captive breeding — zoos breed endangered animals for reintroduction.

Gene banks / seed banks — store DNA and seeds for the future.

Reforestation and field margins — rebuild lost habitats.

High biodiversity = a healthier planet for everyone.

mcqs.q: Which process in the carbon cycle removes CO2 from the atmosphere?
options: Respiration
Combustion
Photosynthesis
Decomposition

mcqs.q: Which bacteria convert nitrogen gas in the air into nitrogen compounds plants can use?
options: Denitrifying bacteria
Nitrogen-fixing bacteria
Decomposers
Nitrifying bacteria

mcqs.q: How do decomposers return carbon to the atmosphere?
options: They respire — breaking down dead organic matter and releasing CO2.
Decomposers release carbon by physically breaking matter into smaller pieces.
Plants only respire at night and only photosynthesise during the day; the processes never overlap.
Decomposers turn dead matter into oxygen and water, with no carbon involved.
Yes — plants respire all the time to release energy; they also photosynthesise when there is light.
Plants only respire at night and only photosynthesise during the day; the processes never overlap.
Plants only photosynthesise and do not respire; respiration is for animals only.
Larger animals always eat the next ones up, and there aren't enough giant animals.

mcqs.q: Why are food chains usually limited to about 4 or 5 trophic levels?
options: Decomposers turn dead matter into oxygen and water, with no carbon involved.
Larger animals always eat the next ones up, and there aren't enough giant animals.
There aren't enough types of animals to fill more trophic levels.
Only ~10 percent of energy is transferred between trophic levels; eventually too little energy remains to support another level.
